title: BLE Advertising and Scanning
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js simulation of a follower robot advertising over Bluetooth Low Energy and a leader robot scanning for it. Students change distance, environment, advertising interval, and scan window, then read a timeline that marks every packet heard or missed, the first-heard time, the follower current, battery life, and a comparison with WiFi current.

educational.topic: Bluetooth Low Energy advertising, scanning, range, and power
learningObjectives: Explain that a scanner hears a packet only while its radio is scanning and the advertiser is in range
Explain how distance and obstacles cause packet loss near the edge of the range
Explain how the advertising interval changes how quickly the scanner finds the advertiser
Explain how the advertising interval changes current draw and battery life compared with WiFi
prerequisites: BLE advertising, scanning, range, and power from Chapter 12

controls.label: Start scan
controls.purpose: Run one ble.gap_scan() and record every advertising packet

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Return to 3 m, Classroom, 100 ms interval, 5000 ms scan

controls.label: Environment
options: Metal shelves in the way (8 m)

controls.label: Follower robot
controls.purpose: Drag left or right to change the distance

equations: advertising events every interval plus a random 0 to 10 ms delay
assumptions: No packets are lost within half the room's range; loss rises to about 50 percent at 80 percent of the range and 100 percent beyond it
The scan window is the whole gap_scan() duration
The scan starts at a random point in the advertising cycle
limitations: Does not model scan interval versus scan window within a scan, or interference from other devices
Current numbers are approximate classroom figures from Chapter 12

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Controlled experiments with a concrete per-packet record
pedagogical.interactionPattern: One scan per button press, with a timeline of heard and missed packets and live power readouts
keyQuestions: Why is a packet sent inside the scan window sometimes still missed?
What happens to packets sent after the scan window ends?
Why does a longer advertising interval make the first hear slower?
How many hours longer does the battery last at 1000 ms than at 100 ms?
commonMisconceptions: A scanner hears every packet from any device in the same room
The advertising interval in gap_advertise() is in milliseconds (it is in microseconds)
BLE and WiFi use about the same power
assessmentOpportunities: Data table from the three one-variable experiments
Exit ticket proposing changes for more reliable discovery
